assessed_by: commit reading via GitHub API; no differential run

discovery.found_by: bbc_e2e mine-commits -> classify -> traversal; surfaced 2026-08-15 as the only open traversal-confirmed beanutils row

the_candidate.message: Add ability to inject properties in non public classes
the_candidate.traversal: confirmed: direct bump 1.9.2 -> 1.9.4 in pom.xml @8b58bbac (2020-03-01), only 5 commits before the adaptation
the_candidate.why_it_looked_strong: Everything structural was right: a direct crossing of the exact boundary, five commits' distance, one production file, and a NEW test added in the same commit. On metadata alone this was the most promising open row in the catalog.

why_excluded.finding: The change replaces commons-beanutils with plain reflection for a reason the project states explicitly, and that reason is not the 1.9.4 behavioural change.
why_excluded.the_diff: PropertyInjector.setProperty(Object value, String name, Object target) calling PropertyUtils.setProperty(target, name, value) becomes setProperty(Object value, Field field, Object target) doing field.setAccessible(true); field.set(target, value). The PropertyUtils import is dropped; the ConvertUtils import stays, so the dependency itself remains.
why_excluded.stated_motive: 'Until now, Easy Props relied on Apache commons-beanutils to set properties on target objects. This requires the object class to be public and to provide a public setter. I believe this is because Apache commons-beanutils is targeted at JavaBeans...'
why_excluded.why_that_is_not_the_break: The JavaBeans constraint the commit removes -- public class, public setter -- held at 1.9.2 exactly as at 1.9.4. It is not a behaviour that changed at the boundary. The 1.9.4 change is narrower: SuppressPropertiesBeanIntrospector.SUPPRESS_CLASS is registered by default, so the property NAMED 'class' stops being introspectable (CVE-2019-10086).
why_excluded.the_new_test_confirms_it: TestPropertyInjectionInNonPublicClass injects into a `private static class MyBean` with a private field and no setter. That would have failed at 1.9.2 too. The test demonstrates a new capability, not a restored one.
why_excluded.why_a_differential_could_not_discriminat: Easy-props injects user-annotated fields by name. None of them is called 'class', so PropertyUtils.setProperty is unaffected by SUPPRESS_CLASS at 1.9.4. State 2 (parent code + 1.9.4) would PASS, and the oracle needs it to fail.

consequence: commons-beanutils-1.9.3-to-1.9.4-classproperty now has ZERO open traversal-confirmed candidates. Its single mined row is dispositioned.
note_on_the_break: This is the second signal that the classproperty break has a very small blast radius, matching the README's screening rule 5: xstream's filter hits every fromXML, whereas beanutils' hits only the property named 'class'. A client has to be reading that specific property to notice at all.
